name: Drawing the Everyday
description:
What can a few lines, a handful of words and a simple visual gag reveal about the world around us?

For over a decade, Rachita Taneja’s Sanitary Panels has used the apparent simplicity of the stick figure and the immediacy of satire to take on questions of gender, sexuality, caste, discrimination, politics and power. Her comics often begin with something seemingly familiar (a news story, an everyday interaction, a social assumption) and reduce it to its essential contradiction, allowing the absurdity of the system behind it to come into view.

In this hands-on workshop, participants will experiment with this process of reduction: taking a complex question around identity or social belonging and translating it into a short comic. Through writing, sequencing, dialogue, visual economy and satire, they will explore how much (and how little) a comic needs to say.

name: Grip, Hold, Pin - Curator walkthrough
description: Join Aayati Sengupta, Curator of Grip, Hold, Pin, for a walkthrough of the exhibition. Through a close reading of the works on view, the walkthrough will explore wrestling as more than a sport—as a site where discipline, kinship, identity and everyday life converge. Drawing on photography, archival material and moving image, Grip, Hold, Pin traces the histories and lived experiences that shape wrestling cultures across India, inviting audiences to consider the relationships between body, labour, tradition and representation.

name: Book Launch - Imposter: The Playful Subversions of Orijit Sen
description:
Join us for a conversation around writer and publisher Sudhanva Deshpande’s new book, Imposter: The Playful Subversions of Orijit Sen. 

Spanning four decades of Orijit Sen’s practice, the book traces the artist’s journey through comics, graphic storytelling, political satire, design and visual culture. From River of Stories, India’s first graphic novel, to the many forms his work has taken since, Sen has continually played with the possibilities of the image and the page. Moderated by Lakshmi Karunakaran, the conversation reflects Orijit’s practice, influences and experiments, and the ideas behind the book.

name: Make Your Own Superhero
description:
What makes a character memorable? How does an idea become a story? And what can a superhero tell us about who we are?

Comic creator Falah Faisal, creator of Musalman, draws on nearly a decade of making comics to explore the building blocks of character, story and identity. Through conversations, prompts and hands-on exercises, participants will develop their own superhero — from their origins and abilities to their world, conflicts and stories.

No drawing skills required. Just bring your imagination and a story waiting to be told.

name: Invisible Inks
description:
In the second edition of Shared Futures, a talk series in conjunction with the exhibition, Beneath the Turning Sky, we take a close look into visual artist Rai’s practice and the different ways her work develops—allowing things to grow and shift along the way, with play, chance and frugality playing an important role in the process.

In conversation with curator Priya Chauhan, she will also touch on the suggestive interactions that are often present of her installations, and the ways these can shape an encounter with the work. Search Party, a video work that forms a pair with the painting that is part of the exhibition will also be screened.
The session will be followed by a hands-on workshop exploring invisible inks and ideas around latency.
Beneath the Turning Sky brings together artists working across painting, sculpture, photography, and textile practices, illuminating contemporary debates around ecology, technology, development, and our relationship with the environment. Through distinct visual languages, the exhibition asks: How might art reshape our collective stewardship of the planet?

Extending these questions beyond the gallery, Shared Futures creates a space for exchange through lectures, conversations, workshops, and other experimental formats. Across these encounters, the series considers what the arts can offer in turbulent times and how creative practices can help forge new ways of thinking, being, and building solidarity.

This series is supported by Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies Foundation
